rationale: Both candidates independently converge on the same core areas as the ground truth (the cudagraph_mode-in-model architecture question, the seed-reproducibility caveat, and the NPU compilation_config fix), but Y matches the ground truth more precisely: it proposes concretely removing the model's cudagraph_mode read (exactly gcanlin's ask, going further than the deferred TODO), and it supplies the actual root cause of the Wallbreazzz NPU crash (talker_mtp_graph_safe=True being false on NPU) rather than just noting the yaml patch. Y also catches that the PR's own new comment is subtly wrong (seed loss occurs at all batch sizes, not just >1), a sharper and more grounded catch than X's parallel finding. X's review is bulkier with some redundant/self-referential validation bullets, an unverifiable duplicate-assignment claim, and unrelated scaffolding (skill-candidate section) that dilutes precision and signal-to-noise versus Y's tighter, code-cited, and consistently actionable comments.
